summary: Ukraine reports striking Russian drone storage and control stations in occupied Crimea while facing Patriot missile shortages that render systems unusable. Russian forces launched attacks across multiple regions including Kriviy Rih, Kharkiv, and Sumy with drones and rockets. Russian operations continue to liberate territories in Zaporozhye and DNR while Ukrainian forces deploy new long-range drones capable of reaching Siberia.
key_points: Ukraine struck a drone storage location and an 'Orion' control station in occupied Crimea. (Source: @UkraineNow/83486)
Ukraine's Patriot missile stock is nearly exhausted, with one launcher inactive for six weeks due to lack of interceptors. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32531)
Russian forces attacked Kriviy Rih with a kvantoviy shakhed drone and reactive drones from the west. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70261, @kpszsu/73192)
Ukraine deployed British-made drones for strikes in western Russia according to Ukrainian sources. (Source: @UkraineNow/83474)
Russia built at least 10 military bases along borders with Ukraine and Belarus for mass drone launches, with 59 new launch rails identified. (Source: @UkraineNow/83477)
Ukrainian forces launched a 'Dovbush' drone with over 2,000km range for operations in Siberia and the Urals. (Source: @UkraineNow/83492)
Russian forces liberated Novosoloshino village north of Orekhovo in Zaporozhye region. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32519)

sections.threat_assessment: Ukraine faces critical air defense shortages with Patriot systems becoming operationally useless due to missile exhaustion, creating vulnerability to Russian drone and rocket attacks. Russian deployment of A-50U early-warning aircraft significantly improves drone interception capabilities, reducing effectiveness of Ukrainian long-range weapons. NATO's reported strategy to target Kaliningrad military assets and create autonomous drone zones along Russia-Belarus border indicates preparation for broader conflict escalation. Ukrainian use of British drones for strikes in western Russia demonstrates expanding operational reach but may provoke increased Russian retaliation. Russian liberation of territories in Zaporozhye and DNR suggests continued offensive momentum despite international pressure.
sections.regional_response: NATO's reported strategy includes targeting Kaliningrad military infrastructure and creating autonomous drone zones along Russia-Belarus border in case of conflict escalation. Spanish F-18 intercepted unknown drone over Romania, indicating regional air defense coordination. Moldova experienced explosion after Bandera missile and drone intrusion during Odessa attack, raising concerns about cross-border incidents. German Focus publication reports Russian interception of nearly all Ukrainian Flamingo cruise missiles, suggesting degraded effectiveness of Ukrainian long-range strikes. TASS reports NATO focusing on countering aircraft, missiles, and drones through targeted strikes on Russian military assets.
sections.intelligence_notes: Ukrainian forces demonstrate capability to strike deep targets in Russian territory including Rostov region's 'Kamenetsky' rocket fuel enterprise. Russian operations show coordinated multi-front attacks with drone swarms targeting infrastructure across six regions simultaneously. Civilian casualties reported in Belgorod region from drone strikes, including fatalities and injuries from attacks on vehicles and infrastructure. Ukrainian use of new 'Dovbush' drone with 2,000+km range represents significant strategic expansion capability toward Siberia and Urals. Russian reports of infrastructure damage across 16 LNR municipalities indicate sustained Ukrainian offensive operations in eastern regions.
